title: Establish granular compatibility metadata and pinning policy for open-model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: As we expand the Model Catalog to include community open weights and experimental variants, the current onboarding metadata is too high-level. Engineers and model ops need precise compatibility signals (quantization-safe, kv-cache-compatible, max-seq, hardware profiles) so runtime can select appropriate kernels and fallbacks automatically. PMs and downstream consumers also need clear pinning semantics to avoid accidental drift when community forks/updates are published.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact, machine- and human-readable metadata schema that covers: model family, architecture version, tokenizer id, max_context, supported quantization profiles, KV cache compatibility, memory footprint estimates (FP16/int8), and explicit incompatible features.
Agree and document a pinning policy that supports three pin types: immutable-hash, semantic-version (major.minor.patch), and floating-latest-with-compat-guard; include fallback behavior for each.

Create a canonical onboarding checklist template that PMs/Eng can use when registering an open model that includes a compatibility score and recommended inference_variant tags (low-latency, cost-optimized, high-accuracy).
Add at least two example model catalog entries (one Llama-derivative and one community chat model) that use the new schema and are validated by the onboarding CI checks.
Runtime team has implemented compatibility flag parsing and a simple policy to refuse 'floating-latest' for Dedicated customers unless explicitly allowed (documented in release notes).
scope: In scope: metadata schema design, pinning policy definition, onboarding checklist, reference examples, CI validation rules, and documentation updates in Confluence and the public onboarding guide. Out of scope: runtime kernel work beyond simple parsing/flagging (deeper runtime scheduling tickets will be created separately), and policy enforcement for existing catalog entries older than 6 months.
non_goals: Do not attempt to auto-convert community model weights into quantized formats in this ticket. Do not change billing or SLA behavior. Do not implement automated rollback across Dedicated pools (separate reliability epic).
decisions: Use a small YAML/JSON metadata blob attached to each catalog entry under key 'compatibility_metadata' to keep machine-parsability and human readability.
Pin types defined: 'hash' (immutable commit/hash), 'semver' (will allow patch upgrades only if compatible), 'floating' (points to latest, allowed only for hosted API by default).
Compatibility will be expressed as explicit booleans and optional notes (e.g., 'kv_cache_compatible': true, 'quantization': ['int8','fp16']).
tradeoffs: Granularity vs. onboarding friction: richer metadata reduces runtime surprises but increases burden on model submitters. We mitigate with templates and auto-detection heuristics in the onboarding CI.
Strict pinning reduces accidental regressions but increases manual work for community model maintainers; offering 'floating' for hosted tier balances discoverability with safety.
Storing hardware memory estimates is imprecise across instance types; we'll provide ranges and a 'measured_on' field to ground numbers.
implementation_notes: PM: publish PRD and onboarding checklist (Confluence) and galvanize two partner teams to act as pilot registrants.
Eng: add a lightweight parser for 'compatibility_metadata' to the catalog service and a validation step in onboarding CI (ENG-2110 will own runtime parsing).
DS/ML: contribute detection heuristics for tokenizer id and architecture family from model files (Lina Zhou will prototype).
Docs: update public onboarding guide and add examples in the developer portal (docs PR linked below).
qa_test_plan: Onboarding CI rejects entries missing required fields (model_family, tokenizer_id, max_context).
Validation job flags incompatible quantization/declarations and surfaces human-readable warnings in the onboarding UI.
Register two pilot models end-to-end and verify the runtime selects the correct inference_variant and does not allow floating pin for Dedicated pilot.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Finalize schema and PRD; collect pilot teams.
Week 1: Implement onboarding CI checks and publish docs; pilot teams register models.
Week 2: Iterate on schema based on pilot feedback; land catalog service parser.
Week 3: Enable enforcement for new entries; communicate change to partners and update release notes.
metrics: % of new catalog entries that include full compatibility_metadata (target 90% after 4 weeks)
Number of runtime incidents due to model incompatibility attributable to missing metadata (target 0 in first month after rollout),
Time-to-onboard (median) for pilot models (target < 3 days for experienced partner).
